title: An assembler, in two passes
task: Write `first_pass(text)`, which returns a dict of `{label: address}` and raises `ValueError` for a label defined twice, and `assemble(text)`, which returns a 32-word memory image: each instruction is `opcode << 5 | address`, and `DATA n` stores `n % 256`. Operands are numbers or labels. `assemble` raises `ValueError` for unknown instructions, undefined labels, addresses outside 0–31, and programs over 32 words.
hints: Re-read "Why two passes": the first pass only counts and records labels; the second turns each line into a word. Then go down the list in "Errors are part of the job": each one needs a check in one of the two functions.

`first_pass`: keep an address counter from 0. For each parsed line, record its label at the current address (raise `ValueError` if the label is already in the dict), and add 1 when the line has a name. `assemble`: write a helper that turns an operand into a number (`None` is 0, a number via `int()`, else a known label, else raise), then make one word per line that has a name.

In `assemble`, loop over the lines again, skipping any with no name. For `DATA`, append `value(...) % 256`. Otherwise, check that the name is in `OPCODES` and that `0 <= v < 32`, then append `OPCODES[name] << 5 | v`. Finally, raise if `len(words) > MEM_SIZE`, and return `words + [0] * (MEM_SIZE - len(words))`.

quiz.q: A program is: a line with only `START:`, then `LOAD X`, `JZ END`, `HALT`, `END: HALT` and `X: DATA 0`. What address does END get?

options.why: Count only the lines that make a word. `START:` on its own doesn't make one, so `LOAD X` is address 0.
`LOAD X` is 0, `JZ END` is 1, `HALT` is 2, so `END: HALT` is 3. The label-only `START:` line takes no word.
That counts every line, including `START:` and the line with `X`. Labels name addresses; they don't take up words.

quiz.q: What does `first_pass` return for this program: `A: DATA 3`, then a line with only `B:`, then `HALT`? Answer as a dict, like `{'X': 2}`.
quiz.why: `A: DATA 3` is word 0. `B:` alone names the next word, which is the `HALT` at address 1.

review.q: A label alone on its line, like `LOOP:`, names which address?

options.text: The address of the next word
options.why: A label-only line makes no word, so the name goes to whatever word comes next.

options.text: Its own line's address, which then holds 0
options.why: A label-only line doesn't produce a word at all.
Only a label before the first word gets 0. In general it's the next word's address.
